primary_sources.title: An Extremal Problem for Polynomials
primary_sources.venue: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 122 (1994), 191--193
primary_sources.exact_source_locator: Printed pp. 191-193 / PDF pp. 1-3: the abstract states the connected-level-set derivative bound; the Chebyshev normalization and properties (i)-(iv) are on printed p. 191 / PDF p. 1; Theorem 1 is on printed p. 192 / PDF p. 2 and gives equality only for f(z)=c^(-n)f_n(cz), |c|=1.
primary_sources.source_artifact_locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 191), Chebyshev definition and properties (i)-(iv); PDF p. 2 (printed p. 192), Theorem 1 and equality characterization; PDF p. 3 (printed p. 193), completion of the uniqueness proof.
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Abstract and Theorem 1, pp. 191-193: for a monic polynomial with connected unit lemniscate, the derivative at a normalized point is bounded by 2^(1/n-1)n^2, with equality only for a rotated/scaled Chebyshev family; pp. 191-192 also list its real negative zeros and critical values ±1.
primary_sources.supports: A directly read primary neighboring sharp connected-lemniscate derivative extremal and the exact Chebyshev equality family, including its real ordered zeros and critical-value normalization.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The present fixed-root-diameter maximin over the least adjacent critical-gap height, the selected chord consumer, or the claimed Lean assurance.

primary_sources.title: Metric Properties of Polynomials
primary_sources.exact_anchor: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 125), Summary: Sections 2--3 study exact real-axis metric quantities when all roots lie on a real interval, while Section 5 turns to components in the unit disk. PDF p. 15 (printed p. 139), immediately after the unit-disk component argument: the paper records that one component contains at least two zeros and states Problem 5 asking whether two zeros can be joined in E by a path of length less than 2.
primary_sources.exact_source_locator: Printed p. 139 / PDF p. 15 / extracted.md lines 594--602: the unit-disk case has a component containing at least two zeros, and the immediately following Problem 5 asks for a path of length less than 2 between listed zeros.
